collections/combining#

Combines Iterating values without materializing them.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let entry = Pair(first: "answer", second: 42);
// entry.first() == "answer"
// entry.second() == 42

Description#

Combines Iterating values without materializing them.

Pair preserves the two original types:

Zipped walks two sources together and stops at the shorter one. It is useful when extra values on either side are intentionally irrelevant:

for Zipped(left: names, right: scores) -> pair {
    output.writeln(pair.first(), ": ", pair.second().string());
}

StrictlyZipped is appropriate when unequal lengths mean corrupt input. Its cursor throws UnequalSizes as soon as available() observes that only one side still has an item.

Chained flattens an Iterating<Iterating<T>> by one level. Sources remain lazy and empty inner sources are skipped with an iterative, stack-safe search:

let all = Chained(origins: pages);
for all -> row {
    output.writeln(row);
}

Every cursor in this module is immutable. successor() returns the next cursor and leaves the receiver at its original item.
